rationale.g1: Revenue Rs 130.12 / 179.66 / 211.36 cr FY24-26 (+38%, +18%); Q1 FY27 Rs 53.5 cr (about 1% ahead of the FY26 run-rate). The issue funds Rs 98.13 cr of new MHE, AWPs and batteries, which at the current asset turn can add a large step of rental revenue over two years. Neutral 15% then 14 / 12 / 10 / 8%; Bear 5-8%; Bull 22% fading to 10%.
rationale.m: EBITDA margin 30.76% in FY26 (EBITDA Rs 65.01 cr), 33.91% in Q1 FY27 (not annualised). Rental EBITDA carries heavy depreciation below it. Neutral 29%; Bear 26%; Bull 32%.
rationale.nwc: Estimate: working capital is not in the tracker data. Rental businesses bill monthly with modest receivables and little inventory beyond trading stock; taken at about 15% of revenue (Rs 32 cr; FY25 about Rs 27 cr). Neutral 15%; Bear 18%; Bull 13%.
rationale.roic: RoNW 34.08% (FY26) on a leveraged equity base; terminal ROIC 15% (Neutral) for a capital-intensive rental fleet.
rationale.capex: D&A Rs 13.4 cr is an estimate: EBITDA 65.01 + other income 0.33 - PBT about 38.9 (PAT 29.16 at 25%) leaves about Rs 26.4 cr for interest and D&A; interest on about Rs 137 cr average debt at 9.5% is about Rs 13.0 cr. Organic capex base Rs 26 cr is an estimate set so that growth capex runs at about 0.4 rupee per rupee of new revenue: the issue's Rs 98.13 cr of fleet spending (Y1-Y2) funds most of the next two to three years' growth, and counting a full asset-turn of organic capex on top would double count it (first run flagged terminal value above 100% of EV). FY26 balance-sheet growth (borrowings +Rs 53.9 cr, net worth +Rs 29.2 cr) suggests gross fleet capex of about Rs 70-80 cr in FY26. IPO capex Rs 98.13 cr (fleet). Net debt taken as gross borrowings Rs 164.08 cr (cash not disclosed, none credited). Fresh issue 49.02 lakh shares = Rs 120.10 cr at Rs 245.
rationale.relative: Relative value uses peer P/E only (w_pb and w_eve set to 0). The RHP peer set as reproduced by trackers is Seemax Resources (P/E 16.07x, RoNW 23.41%) and Leap India (P/E 76.81x, RoNW 6.19%); Leap India is excluded as an outlier. Peer prices and EPS are not reported, so each peer is entered on a per-unit basis (price = its P/E, EPS = 1), which reproduces its P/E without inventing a price.
